findings.state: Briefing -> Saved monitoring rules -> Add monitoring rule -> "Review monitoring rule", when the request is vague, compound ("X and Y"), below 0.70 confidence, or the model's reply cannot be parsed. Same component in the default (v4), ds and oldest Briefing screens.
findings.current: The result block renders only when `parse && parse.parse_succeeded && dispCopy` (AddTriggerFlow.tsx:124). For these requests the Edge Function still answers HTTP 200 with `ok: true` (supabase/functions/briefing-pipeline/index.ts:1356-1362), `parse.parse_succeeded` is false (the prompt tells the model not to commit a parsed_query below 0.70 and to set parse_succeeded=false for compound requests — src/briefing/lib/triggers/parser.ts:99,101; parseTriggerResponse also demotes any success claim without a typed query, parser.ts:250), and the disposition is "clarify_only" (parser.ts:550). `error` stays null because `r.ok` is true (AddTriggerFlow.tsx:67).
findings.problem: Nothing is shown. The button goes back to "Review monitoring rule" and the screen is unchanged: no error, no clarifying questions (ambiguities), no suggested split, no reason. The line written for exactly this case — "This rule needs clarification before it can be enabled. Use the questions below to revise it." — sits inside the parse_succeeded block, so it can only appear for a successful parse under 0.70 confidence, which the prompt forbids. A first-time user who types a vague or two-part request is blocked with no explanation. This is a swallowed validation/partial-result state.
findings.governing: Shared audit brief §5 (states: validation, error, partial result); CLAUDE.md Part II §6 ("loading / error — never blank; never swallowed; never cryptic"); comprehension principle (the user must be told why and what to do next).

findings.state: Briefing -> Add monitoring rule -> "Review monitoring rule" when the model call fails or the Edge Function errors (HTTP 502 "parser call failed: …", 500, 400), or the network is down. Default (v4), ds and oldest screens.
findings.current: `if (error) { return { ok: false, parse: null, disposition: null, error: error.message }; }` (watchlist-client.ts:180-182). For any non-2xx reply supabase-js sets `error.message` to "Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code" (node_modules/@supabase/functions-js/dist/main/types.js:75). The other branches return "parse failed" (line 185) or the raw exception message (line 195). AddTriggerFlow shows the string verbatim (AddTriggerFlow.tsx:67 and :122). Its own fallback "The parser couldn't read that. Try rephrasing." can never render, because `r.error` is always a string when `r.ok` is false.
findings.problem: The fallback for "the language model or network is unavailable" is a transport string. "Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code" does not tell a first-time user whether their wording was the problem or the service failed, or what to do. It also tells them to rephrase nothing — so they will retype a request that was fine. The dead fallback names "the parser", which is internal architecture.
findings.governing: Shared audit brief §5 (fallbacks when AI/network is unavailable; error states); CLAUDE.md Part III §10 (error language: honest, calm, specific, recoverable); COPY_STANDARD.md §2 (literal nouns — no internal component names).
findings.proposed:
In parseTriggerNL keep the technical detail for reportError and return a user-facing message instead:
- transport/HTTP error or thrown exception: "Antaeus could not check that request because the language service did not respond. Your wording was not the problem — try again in a minute."
- `ok !== true` in a 200 reply: same message.
Call `reportError(error, { scope: "watchlist.parseTriggerNL" })` in the `if (error)` branch (today that branch reports nothing).
In AddTriggerFlow.tsx:67 replace the unreachable fallback with the same sentence so no path can print "The parser couldn't read that."

findings.state: Weekly pipeline: enrichment writes event_category for every item; monitoring rules match on it. Affects every single-event and repeated-events rule and the match summaries they produce.
findings.current:
Enrichment schema: `"event_category": string,` with no allowed values, and `"user_relevance_score": number,` with no range (src/briefing/lib/llm/prompts.ts:143 and :149; production copy supabase/functions/briefing-pipeline/llm/_shared.ts:185 and :191).
Rule parser: "3. Map the event to the predefined category list. If it doesn't map cleanly, use category \"any\" and note it." — but the built prompt never prints the list (src/briefing/lib/triggers/parser.ts:96; _shared.ts:243; the schema lines use the placeholder `<category>`). Anything not in EVENT_CATEGORIES is normalised to "any" (parser.ts:329-336).
Matcher: `return lc(item.event_category) === lc(category);` — exact equality against the 18 fixed keys (src/briefing/lib/triggers/matchers.ts:86-89; _shared.ts:719-721).
History: before commit 6d11561 the tested browser prompt carried `// pricing_change | exec_move | funding | layoff_event | product_launch | narrative_shift | partnership | regulatory | other` and `// 0.0-1.0; high when item touches the watchlist…` beside those two fields. The remediation rewrite removed both comments. The production (Deno) copy never had them.
findings.problem: Three pieces of code depend on one vocabulary and neither model is given it. Enrichment is free to write "executive_hire" or "funding" while the rule holds "exec_move" or "funding_round", so a rule for a specific event type may never match; and a rule whose category the parser could not guess becomes "any", so "Alert me when Deel hires a VP of Sales" matches any Deel item whose summary contains the word "sales" (qualifier tokens of three letters or more, matchers.ts:104-115) and is reported as a match. The confirmation the user approved said something narrower. The relevance score has the same problem: the parser clamps to 0–1 (parse-response) but the prompt no longer states the scale, so a model answering on 1–10 or 0–100 is clamped to 1.0 for every item, which feeds cluster qualification and the 0.6 threshold of related-company rules. Verified in code; the model's actual output was not executed, so the size of the effect is an inference. The loss of the two hints from the tested source is a side effect of the language rewrite; production behavior did not change because the mirror already lacked them.
findings.governing: ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/01_OWNER_REQUIREMENTS.md item 7 (scoring/thresholds/recommendation selection, output/API schemas) and "approved evolution versus accidental regression"; deliverables/specs/briefing/signal_console_watchlist_trigger_grammar_v0.1.md §2.1 (EventCategory list) and §6.2 (matching).

Give both models the same vocabulary and restore the scale.

Enrichment prompt, both copies: replace the schema line with `"event_category": one of ` + the 18 EVENT_CATEGORIES keys other than "any", plus "other" — i.e. "exec_move" | "pricing_change" | "product_launch" | "funding_round" | "m_a_event" | "regulatory_action" | "security_incident" | "partnership_announcement" | "integration_added" | "integration_removed" | "leadership_departure" | "layoff_event" | "geographic_expansion" | "vertical_expansion" | "narrative_shift_mention" | "press_coverage" | "patent_filing" | "trust_certification_change" | "other" — and add after the schema: "event_category: choose the single best key from the list; use \"other\" when none fits." and "user_relevance_score: a number from 0.0 to 1.0."
2. Rule-parser prompt, both copies: after PARSE RULES rule 3 print the list: `Event categories: ${EVENT_CATEGORIES.join(", ")}`.
3. Bump PROMPT_VERSION to "enrich-1.2" and TRIGGER_PARSE_PROMPT_VERSION to "trigger-parse-1.1".
4. Tests: assert the enrichment prompt contains every EVENT_CATEGORIES key except "any" and the text "0.0 to 1.0"; assert the rule-parser prompt contains the category list.
Items enriched before the change keep their free-text categories; rules will match them only where the text happens to equal a key.

The rule list, the matches, the cost strip and the opening summary are also read from the live tables without a sample-workspace check (watchlist-client.ts:127-168, cost-client.ts, compose-client.ts), whereas the market analyses are switched to sample content (src/briefing/lib/patterns.ts: `if (isDemoEnv()) return demoSamplePatterns();`).
findings.problem: In the sample workspace the form accepts a request and then tells the user their workspace could not be found and to reload. Reloading cannot help: the feature needs a signed-in workspace and the language service. The message names the wrong cause and the wrong remedy, so a first-time visitor evaluating the product concludes it is broken. If the visitor is signed in while in sample mode, the same code path reads and writes their real workspace's rules from inside the sample (not executed; depends on a session being present).

The heading "Cost this week" does not say what is being costed: a first-time user can read it as a charge to them rather than Antaeus's usage limit for producing their market analysis.

findings.current: `const lead = briefingLead.value; if (!lead) return null; if (!isStaleRun(lead.run_started_at)) return null;` (StaleRunBanner.tsx:41-43). `briefingLead` is the result of parseLeadFromRunData, which returns null unless the latest completed run's data has `compose_lead` or `compose_refusal_reason` (src/briefing/lib/compose-client.ts:36-41). The analyses shown come from the most recent run that produced any (src/briefing/lib/patterns.ts latestRunPatterns), not from the latest run.
findings.problem: The out-of-date warning ("MARKET UPDATES ARE OUT OF DATE … last produced N days ago") can appear only when the newest completed run stored an opening summary. Because of BRIEFING-PIPELINE-006 that key is erased on every run, so the banner cannot appear at all today. Even with that fixed, it stays hidden after exactly the runs that leave the page out of date: when the language service is down every item fails enrichment, no analysis is produced, the compose stage is skipped (compose.ts:60-68) and stores nothing, the run still completes, and the page keeps showing last month's analyses with no warning. The user reads old market analysis as current.

The populated panel shows the pipeline's internals instead of sources: the evidence rows print an internal source key and a relevance number but not the source's title, date or link, although all three are stored in the same record (EvidenceItem.title, url, published_date — synthesis.ts:762-774, saved at :614); "cluster", "anchor", "weighted evidence", "rel", "envelope", "LLM call chain" and "model_v_hash" are engineering terms; "What we challenged" speaks as the system.
